name: annotations/default
description: A process-response plot with data-anchored labels, an event marker, and a warning range. Judge only content inside the plot; ignore headings, descriptions, buttons, controls, and other surrounding UI.

checks.expectation: The plot, annotations, axes, and legend form a coherent plot layout and do not overlap each other in a way that hides their meaning. Annotations touching the plot boundary is acceptable. Do not evaluate content outside the plot.
A continuous pressure-response curve spans the plot. The Process time (s) and Pressure response (units) axes, ticks, grid, and Pressure response legend are visible and readable.

Distinct peak and pressure-drop markers are visibly attached near a high and a low point of the curve, with readable labels. A label box may touch the plot boundary as long as its text is fully readable. Their displayed numeric values may vary with generated sample data and must not be judged for exact equality.

A vertical Valve opened event line and label are visible, together with a translucent horizontal Warning range band and its label. The curve and grid remain distinguishable through or around these annotations.

Within the plot, axis titles, tick labels, legend text, and annotation labels are readable and free of clear raster corruption. Fail only for concrete defects such as square pixel blocks, doubled glyphs, or severe stair-step edges that make plot text materially illegible. Do not compare plot text with headings, buttons, controls, or any text outside the plot. Normal antialiasing, small fonts, rotated text, and backend-specific softness are acceptable.

The plot is not blank, corrupted, reduced to a solid rectangle, or drawn substantially outside its plot area. Annotations are clipped to the plot area by design: an event line, range band, or label box that touches or is partly cut by the plot boundary is acceptable. Fail only if annotation label text itself is cut off, unreadable, or missing.
